learningObjective: Choose between CUDA events and CPU timers when timing a single small CUDA kernel; understand the precision and semantic implications.

canonicalClaims.claim: CUDA events with enable_timing recorded on a specific stream time GPU-side execution of that stream with sub-microsecond resolution and are not perturbed by concurrent work on other streams; CPU timers combined with device-wide synchronize would also charge concurrent work into the measurement.
conditions: Concurrent work exists on other streams during the measurement window.
The goal is to isolate the target kernel's execution.
nonImplications: Does not imply CUDA events are the right tool for coarse timing.
Does not imply event overhead is zero (a few hundred ns per record).

misconceptions.claim: CUDA kernel launches block the host for small kernels.
misconceptions.whyWrong: All CUDA kernel launches are asynchronous with respect to the host regardless of duration.

misconceptions.claim: Device-wide synchronize is the most accurate way to time one stream.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It also drains other streams, over-charging the measurement.
Events can be recorded on any stream.

misconceptions.claim: CPU timers around async launches are always safe with a stream-scoped sync.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They capture host dispatch time too and cannot separate driver overhead from GPU execution.
